agents.note:
US-524 DONE (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 3/8). GPU CMA 64->256 MiB, the third leg of the F-124 freeze work. Commit: feat: [US-524] (implementation e78c51e + this close).

READ THIS FIRST -- I DID NOT WRITE THIS STORY'S CODE THIS ITERATION. I booted into a tree where the implementation was ALREADY COMMITTED (e78c51e, 4 files, 724 insertions) and every piece of bookkeeping was missing: sprint.json still sprint-ready/passes:false, no progress.txt entry, ralph_agents.json still showing me active on US-524. That is the TD-059 stall US-505 documented -- work done, the synchronous gate + close dropped at the END of the iteration -- and it is now the SIXTH sighting across sprints 69-70. The correct move is the one US-505 wrote down: RE-RUN THE GATE, VERIFY, COMMIT THE BOOKKEEPING. Do NOT re-implement. If you boot into a dirty/complete-looking tree matching your taskid, check `git log` for your own story's commit BEFORE writing a line of code.

THE TECHNICAL HEADLINE -- THE AC NAMED THE WRONG SURFACE AND THE BOX SETTLED IT. AC1 says 'boot cmdline/config' and offers config.txt OR cmdline.txt. On the live Pi /proc/cmdline carries NO cma= arg at all: the 64 MiB pool is DEVICE-TREE declared (linux,cma reserved-memory node, visible in dmesg). So a cmdline.txt edit would have been a plausible-looking change competing with the device tree. The real mechanism is the vc4-kms-v3d overlay's OWN cma-256 param (the Pi's /boot/firmware/overlays/README documents cma-64..cma-512). This is the SECOND sprint sighting of US-522's phantom-config shape: when a story is about a value the BOX owns, read the box before believing the AC's nouns.

WHY config.txt AND NOT cmdline.txt, beyond mechanism -- RECOVERABILITY, and it is the principle I would carry forward: when two mechanisms are both correct, pick the one whose failure you can recover from. A bad overlay param makes the firmware skip the overlay -> dark display, SSH STILL UP, fixable remotely. A malformed cmdline.txt can break root= and leave an UNBOOTABLE HEADLESS box -- a car-mounted Pi with no keyboard. Equal-correctness options are not equal-blast-radius options. A guard pins that cmdline.txt is never touched.

AC1's SECOND HALF ('whether deploy-pi.sh can write it within scope') = YES, so the conditionalOutcome escape hatch ('emit a one-line CIO ops instruction instead of forcing it into the deploy script -- do not half-apply') was correctly NOT taken. There is an exact precedent: step_enforce_eeprom_power_off_on_halt (US-253) is a standalone sudo'd idempotent script re-asserted on EVERY deploy. step_set_gpu_cma mirrors it and is ordered directly after it, both AFTER sync_tree so the script exists on the Pi. Re-asserting every deploy is the POINT, not redundancy: config.txt is OS-shipped and rewritable out-of-band by rpi-update / an image upgrade / raspi-config -- the same unmanaged-boot-surface class as US-522's /etc/chromium.d note (A-16).

WHAT I ADDED THAT THE ORIGINAL COMMIT LACKED: I ran set-gpu-cma.sh against a COPY of the live Pi's REAL config.txt, not only my own synthetic fixtures. That is what makes the section-scoping logic defensible rather than theoretical -- the REAL file contains [cm4], [cm5] (with its own dtoverlay=dwc2,dr_mode=host) and [all]. config.txt is SECTION-SCOPED: a [cm4]/[pi4]/[HDMI:0] header makes every following line conditional until the next header, so a naive grep+append could land in a section the firmware IGNORES on a Pi 5 and then report SUCCESS. Only the implicit top-level, [all] and [pi5] are valid targets. Result against the real file: applied at line 26 -> dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-256; idempotent no-op on re-run; backup pristine; and the [cm5] dwc2 overlay UNTOUCHED, which is the actual proof it does not spray cma- onto unrelated overlays. Mutated a COPY only -- the Pi's boot config was never modified (read-only cat was the sole remote op) -- and I deleted all four temp files and VERIFIED the deletion (US-522's cleanup lesson: my predecessor's cleanup died with the ssh session and never ran).

OWED, AND NOT FAKED: AC2 / validationCriteria ('post-boot CmaTotal ~262144 kB') needs the deploy PLUS A REBOOT, and deploying is PM-owned (handbook 13). I probed read-only and the honest current state is: Pi STILL at CmaTotal 65536 kB, overlay line still bare, and ~/obd2/deploy/set-gpu-cma.sh NOT YET on the box -- the deploy has not run. The drill is deploy -> reboot -> `grep CmaTotal /proc/meminfo`. The script prints exactly that command and the expected number, and says REBOOT REQUIRED rather than implying the pool was raised immediately.

HONEST BOUND -- DO NOT OVERREAD A GREEN US-524: this is Atlas RCA #4, OPTIONAL HEADROOM, explicitly NOT a standalone fix. US-522's --disable-gpu is the freeze fix. And the two INTERACT: with --disable-gpu the kiosk renders in SOFTWARE, so a bigger CMA pool may show no measurable chromium effect at all. Shipping the mechanism is the deliverable; claiming a benefit nobody measured is not.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP: tests/deploy/test_set_gpu_cma.py 8 passed with ZERO SKIPS -- check that, because all 35 bash assertions reach pytest through ONE wrapper test gated on shutil.which('bash'), so on a bash-less box it SKIPS and `-q` renders it as an unremarkable 's' while the entire behavioural catalog quietly stops running. I also ran the .sh directly: 35 passed / 0 failed over 12 scenarios. FULL tests/deploy 405 passed (deploy-pi.sh changed, same posture as US-522/523). ruff clean on the touched Python file.

PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE, BOTH IN THIS SPRINT: tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py = TD-073 = US-529. TD-075's 10 project-wide ruff errors outside touched files mean `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 on a clean tree, so lint was applied per-touched-file. `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which reads like a pass.

HARNESS GOTCHAS that cost me time, for the next agent: `VAR=x cmd` env-prefixes AND PowerShell `$env:X=...` are BOTH blocked here, and `>` redirection outside the working dir is blocked. To exercise a script behind an env-var seam, write a throwaway probe .sh that exports the var, run it, delete it, verify. Compound `&&` chains re-prompt -- one command per call. And pass an explicit long timeout so a slow-SMB gate is not auto-backgrounded (backgrounded = TD-059 by accident).

NEXT UP is US-525 (splash render / 401). Read its AC1 carefully: Atlas already established the 401 on bare /boot and /shutdown is BY-DESIGN and US-501's _injectHtml is EXONERATED, so the story's FIRST job is to find what actually REQUESTS those routes before assuming the 401 is even on the render path. Weakening _tokenOk on any route is an Atlas BLOCK (TD-067).
